# Claude tools

115 tools that Claude calls to edit a video. They are defined in [engine/claude/tools.ts](../../engine/claude/tools.ts) and exposed with `toAnthropicTools()` in Messages API format. Run them with `executeTool(session, name, input)`. Inputs are validated against the schemas below, and errors come back as `isError` results instead of exceptions.

Tools marked **edits** change the project, record an undo step and notify the live preview. Tools marked **read-only** only inspect or render.

## Inspect & project

**read-only**. Get a readable summary of the current edit (assets, clips with timeline times, layers, audio, captions) plus validation issues. Call this first and whenever you need to re-orient.

| `includeJson` | boolean |  | `false` | Also return the raw project JSON |

### undo

**edits**. Undo the last edit.

_No parameters._

### redo

**edits**. Redo the last undone edit.

_No parameters._

### clean_up_media

**edits**. Tidy the project's media: assets that are the same file content (imported twice, or copies under other names) become one, and assets nothing in the edit uses are removed (pass keep for ones you still plan to use). deleteFiles also deletes files in the project's media folder that no asset uses any more (this cannot be undone; ask the user first).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `removeUnused` | boolean |  | `true` |  |
| `keep` | string[] |  | `[]` | Asset ids to keep even if unused |
| `deleteFiles` | boolean |  | `false` | Also delete unused files in <project>/media |

### review_edit

**read-only**. Check the edit for what a viewer notices, with timeline times, without changing anything. It renders sample frames and the audio mix in one pass and reports: text that is hard to read against the picture, runs off the frame, or collides with captions or other text (text); text and captions where TikTok, Reels and Shorts put their buttons and captions (safe-zones); black, frozen or repeated footage (frames); words cut off at an edit, doubled caption words, captions over silence, and speech the transcript skipped (speech); loudness off target, peaks, and music too loud under the voice (audio); screen color a chroma key left behind (key); highlights or shadows the grade clipped, skin pushed off the skin line, banding the grade brought out in skies and walls, each against the same frame without the grade (grade); model mattes that flicker, tracks that pinned layers and masks follow where they are unsure, and a replaced sky sliding against the scenery (vfx). It also finds text and captions covering a face (local face detection). Run it before render_video and after big changes, fix what it finds, then run it again.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `checks` | "text" \| "safe-zones" \| "frames" \| "speech" \| "audio" \| "key" \| "grade" \| "vfx"[] |  |  | Only these checks (default all) |
| `platform` | "auto" \| "tiktok" \| "reels" \| "shorts" \| "vertical" \| "none" |  | `"auto"` | Safe zones to check: auto = all three vertical apps for a portrait video, none for landscape |
| `loudnessTarget` | number |  | `-14` | Integrated loudness to aim for in LUFS: -14 social video and YouTube, -16 podcasts (≥ -30, ≤ -8) |

### offer_choices

**read-only**. Let the user choose when taste decides, instead of deciding for them: a narration voice (play the files preview_voice made), a music track, a sound effect, or a look (show frames you rendered with each option, e.g. render_frame after each title style, then undo). The app shows the options as cards they can play or view and pick. Offer 2 to 6, each with a short label. End your turn right after calling it: their pick arrives as their next message, and then you apply it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `question` | string | yes |  | What to choose, e.g. 'Which voice should narrate?' |
| `options` | { label, description, audio, image }[] | yes |  |  |

### add_clip

**edits**. Add a clip to the primary track (clips play back-to-back). Use `in`/`duration` (source seconds) to trim. Images/colors need a duration. Add shots, not whole recordings: pick the moment worth showing, and for a montage or music video add many short shots that alternate sources and framings, timed to the bar grid of the music.

| `focus` | { x, y } |  |  | Crop focus for fit cover: x 0 = keep left edge, 1 = right edge |
| `focus.x` | number | yes |  | Horizontal center, 0 = left edge, 1 = right edge |
| `focus.y` | number | yes |  | Vertical center, 0 = top edge, 1 = bottom edge |

### split_edit

**edits**. Make a J or L cut at the cut into a primary clip, so sound and picture change at different moments (standard in interviews and talking heads). 'j': the clip's sound starts early, heard under the end of the previous shot (we hear the next speaker before we see them). 'l': the previous clip's sound carries on under the start of this one (we keep hearing the speaker while cutting to a reaction or b-roll). The other clip's sound is muted where they overlap; captions follow the sound. seconds 0 removes it. Needs footage beyond the cut (trimmed-off source).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | yes |  | The clip right after the cut |
| `type` | "j" \| "l" | yes |  |  |
| `seconds` | number | yes |  | How far the sound leads (j) or trails (l) the picture cut; 0.5-2 is typical (≥ 0, ≤ 10) |

### freeze_frame

**edits**. Hold one frame of the video still for a few seconds (a freeze-frame, e.g. for a 'that's me' title or a dramatic beat). The frame at the given timeline time is held there and the rest of the clip continues after it, so the video gets longer by seconds. The still keeps the clip's fit, crop and effects. Add a title or effect on top afterwards.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `time` | number | yes |  | Timeline seconds of the frame to hold (≥ 0) |
| `seconds` | number |  | `2` | (≥ 0.1, ≤ 30) |

### set_speed

**edits**. Speed up or slow down a primary clip or an audio clip (0.25-4; 0.5 = half speed slow motion, 2 = double speed). Audio keeps its pitch. The clip covers the same source footage, so it gets shorter or longer on the timeline and later clips move. Captions follow automatically. Slowing a video clip below its footage's frame rate turns on smooth motion (see interpolate), so frames are made in between instead of repeated; smooth: false keeps repeated frames.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes |  | Clip id or audio clip id |
| `speed` | number | yes |  | (≥ 0.25, ≤ 4) |
| `smooth` | boolean |  |  | Video clips: make in-between frames where the footage runs out (default: yes when it does) |

### speed_ramp

**edits**. Change a clip's speed over time: fast, then slow motion on the moment that matters, then back (a speed ramp). Keyframes give the speed at moments of the clip's FOOTAGE (seconds from its in point, as in its source), with easing into each; the speed holds before the first and after the last. Example, a 2x run-up into slow motion: [{time: 0, speed: 2}, {time: 1.5, speed: 2}, {time: 2, speed: 0.4}, {time: 3, speed: 0.4}, {time: 3.4, speed: 1}]. The clip keeps the same footage, so its length on the timeline changes and later clips move. Sound follows with its pitch kept; captions and cuts follow too. Pass null to go back to the clip's steady speed. Slow parts below the footage's frame rate get smooth motion (see interpolate) unless smooth is false.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | yes |  |  |
| `keyframes` | { time, speed, easing }[] \| null | yes |  |  |
| `smooth` | boolean |  |  | Make in-between frames where the footage runs out (default: yes when it does) |

### interpolate

**edits**. Smooth motion for video clips that show more frames than their footage has: slow motion and speed ramps below the footage's frame rate, or a lower frame rate than the edit's (24 fps footage in a 60 fps edit). Without it those frames repeat and motion stutters; with it a model on this machine (RIFE, a 21 MB model downloads once) makes the frames in between, only the ones the edit shows. About half a second a frame at 1080p with a graphics card and several seconds without, done once and cached; reports per clip how many frames were made. set_speed and speed_ramp turn it on by themselves when they slow a clip that far; this prepares the frames now (so previews show them too) or turns it off. Check fast movement and edges where things cross (hands, spokes, water) with render_preview; a cut inside a clip is never blended across.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipIds` | string[] |  |  | Clips (default: every primary video clip with smooth motion on, or that shows frames its footage lacks) |
| `off` | boolean |  |  | Turn smooth motion off for these clips (frames repeat again) |

### set_transition

**edits**. Set the transition into a clip (or between all clips with all=true). type 'none' removes it. sound: true adds the sound that matches the motion (swoosh for slides and wipes, whoosh for whips and zooms, glitch for glitch cuts), peaking in the middle of the transition; or name a sound effect. Changing or removing the transition replaces its sound. Use them sparingly: hard cuts carry most edits; put transitions on phrase changes or shifts in place or mood, keep to one or two kinds per video, and center them on a beat when there is music.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string |  |  |  |
| `all` | boolean |  | `false` |  |
| `type` | string | yes |  |  |
| `duration` | number |  | `0.5` | (> 0, ≤ 5) |
| `origin` | { x, y } |  |  | Start point for circlereveal (frame fractions), e.g. the presenter's hand |
| `origin.x` | number | yes |  | Horizontal center, 0 = left edge, 1 = right edge |
| `origin.y` | number | yes |  | Vertical center, 0 = top edge, 1 = bottom edge |
| `sound` | boolean \| string |  | `false` | true = the transition's matching sound, or a sound effect id |

### create_effect

**edits**. Make your own reusable visual effect from an FFmpeg filter chain and save it in the project by name; then add it anywhere with add_effect (type 'custom', params { name }). Use it for looks the catalog lacks: per-pixel math with geq (X, Y, W, H, T and functions like sin, hypot, st/ld), color math, displacement-free distortions (lenscorrection, v360, perspective), glitches (rgbashift, chromashift, noise), trails (lagfun, tmix), edge and comic looks (edgedetect, posterize via lutrgb, elbg). Allowed filters: eq, hue, curves, colorbalance, colorchannelmixer, colorlevels, colortemperature, colorcontrast, colorcorrect, colorize, vibrance, selectivecolor, huesaturation, exposure, lutrgb, lutyuv, lut, negate, monochrome, grayworld, normalize, pseudocolor, geq, gblur, boxblur, avgblur, dblur, smartblur, unsharp, cas, convolution, edgedetect, sobel, prewitt, roberts, deband, gradfun, bilateral, median, vignette, noise, chromashift, rgbashift, pixelize, elbg, posterize, kirsch, colorhold, chromakey, colorkey, hsvhold, hsvkey, lenscorrection, rotate, hflip, vflip, transpose, crop, scale, pad, perspective, shear, swaprect, v360, fillborders, tmix, lagfun, tblend, deflicker, fade, format, setsar, null. The chain is test-rendered before saving, so mistakes come back as errors. Saving a name again replaces it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |  | Short name, e.g. 'neon edges' |
| `filter` | string | yes |  | Comma-separated FFmpeg filters for one stream |
| `description` | string |  |  | What it looks like, for later |

### animate_effect

**edits**. Change an effect's settings over time: a blur that ramps up into a transition, a grade that shifts from cold to warm, a vignette that closes in. The effect must already be on the target (add_effect, color_adjust, retouch). Each keyframe sets some of the effect's settings at a time (timeline seconds, or seconds into the clip or layer with relative), with easing into it; the settings hold before the first keyframe and after the last. Numbers move smoothly between keyframes; other settings switch half way. A ramp runs up to six copies of the effect, so it costs more to render. Pass null to remove the keyframes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes |  | Clip id, media layer id, or "global" |
| `type` | string | yes |  | Effect type on the target, e.g. blur, color, vignette |
| `keyframes` | { time, params, easing }[] \| null | yes |  |  |
| `relative` | boolean |  | `false` | Times count from the clip's or layer's start instead of the timeline |

## People & faces

### retouch

**edits**. Retouch people in a clip, a media layer, every clip, or the whole video. beauty: skin smoothing that keeps edges sharp, plus brighten and warmth, on the whole frame or only inside a face region. beauty region "faces" retouches only the faces and follows every face frame by frame (found on this machine; primary video clips only), which is the best choice when people move. backgroundBlur: portrait mode, blurring everything but the subject. subject "person" follows the real outline of the person on every frame (cut out on this machine; primary video clips only), which is the best choice when people move. replaceBackground: a solid backdrop color behind the person, using the same cutout (no green screen needed). Ellipses instead: region "face" or subject "face" place one from the faces found in each clip (covering where the face moves), or give one yourself (center x, y and width, height as frame fractions); an ellipse stays put for the whole clip. Check the result with render_frame. Settings merge into the target's existing retouch, so you can tweak one value at a time. Pass false to remove one.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes |  | A clip id, a media layer id, "all-clips", or "global" (whole video) |
| `beauty` | false \| { smooth, brighten, warmth, region } |  |  |  |
| `backgroundBlur` | false \| { amount, subject, feather, dim } |  |  |  |
| `replaceBackground` | false \| { color, mix, feather } |  |  |  |

### detect_faces

**read-only**. Find and follow the faces in primary clips (or in a source asset), on this machine (a small model downloads once). For each person: when they are on screen (timeline times), where the face sits in the edit's frame after the clip's crop, and how far it moves. Use it to place titles and callouts away from faces, to check what a 9:16 crop keeps (then reframe), and for retouch with region or subject "face". Zooms and shakes from effects are not followed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string |  |  | Clip id, asset id (source times and source frame), or omit for every primary clip |
| `fps` | number |  | `2` | Frames checked per second (≥ 0.5, ≤ 10) |

### reframe

**edits**. Point each clip's crop at the person in it, for fit cover when the source shape differs from the video (16:9 footage in a 9:16 video). It finds the faces in each clip. By default the crop is fixed: it keeps the main face's whole path in frame, or its usual spot when it moves more than the crop can show. With follow, the crop pans with the person like a camera operator (focus keyframes, smoothed).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipIds` | string[] |  |  | Clips to reframe (default: every cover-fit clip whose source shape differs) |
| `follow` | boolean |  | `false` | Pan the crop with the person over time instead of a fixed crop |

### follow_face

**edits**. Make a layer (a name label, a callout, an arrow, a sticker) follow a person on screen: it finds the main face in the clips under the layer and sets position keyframes beside it (above, below, left, right, or on it), smoothed so it glides rather than jitters. The layer stays inside the frame. Where no face is found it holds its last spot.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `layerId` | string | yes |  |  |
| `clipId` | string |  |  | Clip to follow (default: the primary clips under the layer) |
| `side` | "above" \| "below" \| "left" \| "right" \| "on" |  | `"above"` |  |
| `gap` | number |  | `0.02` | Space between the face and the layer (frame fraction) (≥ 0, ≤ 0.3) |

### update_layer

**edits**. Change a layer's properties (text, start, duration, position, style, size, opacity, animations…). Text style is merged. Media and graphic layers take behindSubject: true to go behind the people in the video. They also take blend: "screen" or "add" for fire, sparks, light leaks and flares shot on black (the black disappears), "multiply" for textures on white, "overlay" or "softlight" for texture and contrast, also lighten, darken, colordodge, difference, and "normal" to undo. Check a blend with render_frame on a dark and a bright moment.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `layerId` | string | yes |  |  |
| `patch` | object | yes |  |  |

### reorder_layer

**edits**. Change which layer draws on top. Layers draw in list order (later on top); text and shapes always draw above media overlays. Put a layer directly below or above another layer (e.g. a dimming shape below a title), or at an index.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `layerId` | string | yes |  |  |
| `below` | string |  |  | Layer id to place it directly under |
| `above` | string |  |  | Layer id to place it directly over |
| `toIndex` | integer |  |  | 0 = bottom (≥ 0) |

### remove_layer

**edits**. Delete a layer (text, media overlay or shape). To remove a whole component, remove each of its layers.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `layerId` | string | yes |  |  |

### animate_layer

**edits**. Move, scale, turn or fade a layer over time with keyframes (text, shapes and media overlays): a label that slides along with a product, a logo that grows, a title that drifts. Give a list of keyframes per property; each has a time (timeline seconds, or seconds into the layer with relative), a value, and easing into it from the previous keyframe (default ease-in-out; linear for steady motion). Before the first keyframe a property holds its first value, after the last its last. Pass null to remove a property's keyframes. Entrance and exit animations still play. To follow a person, use follow_face.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `layerId` | string | yes |  |  |
| `position` | { time, x, y, easing }[] \| null |  |  | Center of the layer (frame fractions) |
| `scale` | { time, value, easing }[] \| null |  |  | Size multiplier (1 = its own size) |
| `rotation` | { time, value, easing }[] \| null |  |  | Degrees clockwise |
| `opacity` | { time, value, easing }[] \| null |  |  | Multiplies the layer's opacity |
| `rotateX` | { time, value, easing }[] \| null |  |  | 3D tilt in degrees, media and graphic layers (+ tips the top away; 90 is edge-on) |
| `rotateY` | { time, value, easing }[] \| null |  |  | 3D turn in degrees, media and graphic layers (+ turns the right side away; 0 to 360 is a full spin) |
| `relative` | boolean |  | `false` | Times count from the layer's start instead of the timeline |

## Graphics, icons & fonts

### create_graphic

**edits**. Design your own graphic in SVG and put it on the video: lower thirds, title cards, styled or 3D-looking text, UI mockups (app screens, notifications, chat bubbles, buttons, progress bars), charts, badges, stickers, frames, logos, patterns. Anything SVG can draw works: paths, gradients, patterns, masks, clip paths, strokes, any installed font (font-family by name; see list_fonts and install_fonts), and filters for drop shadows (feDropShadow), glows, blurs, inner shadows, long shadows and extrusions (stacked offset copies). The <svg> needs a viewBox; it is drawn at width (fraction of frame width) with the viewBox's shape, centered at position. Animate it with {{ expression }} placeholders anywhere in the SVG (attributes, transforms, colors' opacity, text positions), evaluated on every frame. Variables: t (seconds from the graphic's start), p (progress 0..1 over its duration), d (duration), n (frame number), w and h (canvas size in pixels), PI. Operators: + - * / % ** and parentheses, comparisons < <= > >= == != (1 or 0), and cond ? a : b. Functions: sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2 abs min max pow sqrt exp log floor ceil round sign clamp(x,a,b) lerp(a,b,u) step(edge,x) smooth(a,b,x) ease(u) easeIn(u) easeOut(u) easeInOut(u) back(u) elastic(u) bounce(u) (easings take 0..1), seg(t,a,b) (0..1 progress of t from a to b), wave(t,period) (0..1 sine), rad(deg), deg(rad). Example: <rect width="{{ 600*easeOut(seg(t,0,0.8)) }}" .../> grows a bar in 0.8 s; transform="rotate({{ 360*p }} 100 100)" spins once. For depth, turn the whole graphic in 3D with rotateX/rotateY (animate them with animate_layer). The layer also takes animate_layer keyframes, entrance/exit animations and layer effects like any overlay. Check the result with render_frame.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `svg` | string | yes |  | SVG markup with a viewBox, optionally with {{ expression }} placeholders |
| `start` | number | yes |  | (≥ 0) |
| `duration` | number | yes |  | (> 0) |
| `width` | number |  | `0.5` | Width as a fraction of frame width (> 0, ≤ 2) |
| `position` | { x, y } |  |  | Center (frame fractions, default the middle) |
| `position.x` | number | yes |  | Horizontal center, 0 = left edge, 1 = right edge |
| `position.y` | number | yes |  | Vertical center, 0 = top edge, 1 = bottom edge |
| `opacity` | number |  |  | (≥ 0, ≤ 1) |
| `blend` | "normal" \| "screen" \| "add" \| "multiply" \| "overlay" \| "softlight" \| "lighten" \| "darken" \| "colordodge" \| "difference" \| "addlight" \| "screenlight" |  |  | screen or add for glows and light drawn on black; see update_layer |
| `shadow` | number |  |  | Extra soft drop shadow under the whole graphic, in pixels (≥ 0) |
| `rotateX` | number |  |  | 3D tilt in degrees (≥ -89, ≤ 89) |
| `rotateY` | number |  |  | 3D turn in degrees (≥ -89, ≤ 89) |
| `perspective` | number |  |  | Camera distance in widths for 3D (default 2) (≥ 0.5, ≤ 20) |
| `behindSubject` | boolean |  |  | Put the layer behind the people in the video (smoke, light beams, props and set pieces behind a dancer or presenter), found frame by frame in the finished picture. The first render after changing the clips takes longer while it looks for them |
| `animationIn` | { type, duration, easing } |  |  |  |
| `animationIn.type` | string | yes |  | Animation id from the animations catalog, e.g. 'fade', 'pop', 'slide-up' |
| `animationIn.duration` | number |  | `0.4` | (> 0, ≤ 10) |
| `animationIn.easing` | "linear" \| "ease-in" \| "ease-out" \| "ease-in-out" |  | `"ease-out"` |  |
| `animationOut` | { type, duration, easing } |  |  |  |
| `animationOut.type` | string | yes |  | Animation id from the animations catalog, e.g. 'fade', 'pop', 'slide-up' |
| `animationOut.duration` | number |  | `0.4` | (> 0, ≤ 10) |
| `animationOut.easing` | "linear" \| "ease-in" \| "ease-out" \| "ease-in-out" |  | `"ease-out"` |  |
| `label` | string |  |  |  |

### list_fonts

**read-only**. List the font families text can use: the ones added with install_font, the bundled ones (Arimo, Archivo Black, Gelasio, Anton, Cousine, Comic Neue: the same on every computer, so prefer them and added fonts over system fonts) and the ones installed on this computer. Use the family name exactly as listed in a text style's fontFamily.

| `query` | string |  |  | Filter by name, e.g. 'mono' or 'sans' |

### install_font

**read-only**. Add a font from Google Fonts (all open-licensed, free for video), e.g. 'Montserrat', 'Bebas Neue', 'Playfair Display', 'Inter', 'Anton'. It downloads once into the fonts folder and every render can use it as fontFamily.

| `family` | string | yes |  | Family name as on fonts.google.com |

| `italic` | boolean |  | `false` |  |

### install_fonts

**read-only**. Install many Google Fonts families at once: whole packs and/or a list of families. Packs: sans (30: Inter, Montserrat, Poppins, Roboto, Open Sans…); display (35: Bebas Neue, Anton, Oswald, Archivo Black, Black Ops One…); serif (20: Playfair Display, Merriweather, Lora, DM Serif Display, Cormorant Garamond…); script (20: Pacifico, Lobster, Dancing Script, Great Vibes, Satisfy…); handwriting (15: Caveat, Permanent Marker, Shadows Into Light, Indie Flower, Amatic SC…); mono (12: JetBrains Mono, Fira Code, Roboto Mono, Space Mono, IBM Plex Mono…). Families already installed are skipped. Installed fonts work in text styles, captions and create_graphic SVG (font-family by name).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `packs` | "sans" \| "display" \| "serif" \| "script" \| "handwriting" \| "mono"[] |  |  |  |
| `families` | string[] |  |  | More families by name as on fonts.google.com |

### make_thumbnail

**read-only**. Make a thumbnail image (YouTube style: a frame of the video, punchier color, a big bold title of 2-5 words). The frame comes from the edit at time (without its own titles and captions). The title goes on the side away from the faces in the frame (side auto), wrapped onto short lines. Saved as a 1280x720 JPEG for landscape projects (YouTube's size), else the project's size. Look at the result and try another time or title if it does not read at a glance.

| `side` | "auto" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top" \| "bottom" |  | `"auto"` |  |
| `color` | string |  | `"#FFFFFF"` | Title color |
| `accentColor` | string |  | `"#FFD000"` | Subtitle box color |
| `punch` | number |  | `0.6` | How much to boost contrast and color (0 = frame as is) (≥ 0, ≤ 1) |

### set_volume

**edits**. Set the volume of a primary clip, an audio clip, a media layer, or the whole mix (target "master"). volume is a multiplier: 1 = original, 0.5 = about -6 dB, 2 = about +6 dB, 0 = silent (max 4). Or give db instead. muted applies to primary clips.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes |  | Clip id, audio clip id, media layer id, or "master" |
| `volume` | number |  |  | (≥ 0, ≤ 4) |
| `db` | number |  |  | Volume in decibels relative to the original level (0 = original), instead of volume (≥ -60, ≤ 12) |
| `muted` | boolean |  |  |  |

### enhance_audio

**edits**. One-call cleanup for speech: removes hum, reduces background noise, enhances the voice (clarity, presence, de-essing, compression, even levels) and optionally normalizes loudness. Target a clip, an audio clip (e.g. a voice-over), a media layer, "all-clips", or "master". Calling it again replaces the previous cleanup settings on the target.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes |  | Clip id, audio clip id, media layer id, "all-clips", or "master" |
| `noiseReduction` | number |  | `40` | Background noise reduction 0-100 (0 = off) (≥ 0, ≤ 100) |
| `noiseFloor` | number |  |  | Level of the noise in dB (default -35); raise toward -25 for loud hiss (≥ -70, ≤ -20) |
| `voice` | number |  | `60` | Voice enhancement strength 0-100 (0 = off) (≥ 0, ≤ 100) |
| `removeHum` | 50 \| 60 |  |  | Remove mains hum at 50 Hz or 60 Hz |
| `normalize` | number |  |  | Normalize loudness to this LUFS target (-14 for social video, -16 for podcasts) (≥ -30, ≤ -8) |

### add_audio_effect

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes |  | Clip id, audio clip id, media layer id, or "master" |
| `type` | string | yes |  |  |
| `params` | object |  |  |  |

### remove_audio_effect

**edits**. Remove an audio effect (by type) from a clip, audio clip, media layer or "master".

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes |  |  |
| `type` | string | yes |  |  |

## Sound map, beats & moments

### analyze_audio

**read-only**. Map the sound of a recording without a transcript: where someone is speaking, where it is silent, where music or other sound plays, loud moments (claps, bangs, laughs) and the beat. Give an assetId for source times (best for raw footage, before cutting), or omit it to map every primary clip on the timeline. Returns a timeline of segments and a picture (waveform with a colored band: green speech, blue music, orange other sound, dark silence, red loud moments). Labels come from a local sound model (no speech recognition): sung music is marked 'music with vocals', and other sounds are named, like 'sound (dog)' or 'sound (siren)'. Treat '(unsure)' segments with care and check with render_frame or your own judgement. Use the times with remove_silences, assemble_from_source, split_clip, add_sound_effect and beat_sync.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string |  |  | Asset to analyze (source times); omit for the current timeline |
| `start` | number |  |  | Source seconds to start at (asset mode) (≥ 0) |
| `end` | number |  |  | Source seconds to stop at (asset mode) (> 0) |
| `image` | boolean |  | `true` | Also return the sound map picture |

### remove_silences

**edits**. Cut dead air out of footage: removes silent stretches (or everything that is not speech) from primary clips, leaving short padding. Works without a transcript; with one, words are never cut into, so transcribe first when you can. Each kept part becomes its own clip (jump cuts). Layers, music and captions stay in sync. Run analyze_audio first to see what will go.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string |  |  | Only cut clips of this asset (default: every clip with sound) |
| `keep` | "speech" \| "music" \| "sound"[] |  | `["speech","music","sound"]` | What counts as worth keeping; ["speech"] also removes music, noise and other non-speech sound |
| `minSilence` | number |  | `0.5` | Only remove gaps at least this long (seconds) (≥ 0.1) |
| `padding` | number |  | `0.15` | Seconds kept before and after each kept part (≥ 0, ≤ 1) |

### detect_scenes

**edits**. Find shot changes (cuts between camera angles or scenes) in a video asset. With split=true, the primary clips using it are split at every change inside them, so each shot becomes its own clip to trim, reorder, grade or give a transition.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | yes |  |  |
| `threshold` | number |  | `0.3` | 0.3 finds clear cuts; 0.15-0.2 also finds gentle ones (≥ 0.05, ≤ 0.9) |
| `split` | boolean |  | `false` |  |

### detect_beats

**read-only**. Find the tempo and beat times of music: an audio clip (times on the timeline) or an asset (source times). Use them to cut, punch, shake or flash on the beat (beat_sync does this for you).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes |  | Audio clip id (timeline times) or asset id (source times) |

### beat_sync

**edits**. Edit to the music's beat. action 'cuts' moves every cut between primary clips onto the nearest beat; an effect action (zoomPunch, impactShake, flashHits, vibrate) puts that effect on the beats. Choose every Nth beat (2 or 4 for calmer pacing; downbeats=true for bar starts only) and an optional time window. sound adds a sound effect on the same beats.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes |  | Music audio clip id, or an asset on the primary track |
| `action` | "cuts" \| "zoomPunch" \| "impactShake" \| "flashHits" \| "vibrate" | yes |  |  |
| `every` | integer |  | `1` | (≥ 1, ≤ 16) |
| `downbeats` | boolean |  | `false` | Use only bar starts |
| `start` | number |  |  | Timeline seconds to start at (≥ 0) |
| `end` | number |  |  | Timeline seconds to stop at (> 0) |
| `params` | object |  |  | Effect params, e.g. {amount: 0.12} |
| `sound` | string |  |  | Sound effect to add on the same beats, e.g. 'hit' |
| `minClip` | number |  | `0.4` | cuts: shortest clip allowed (≥ 0.1) |

### add_moment_effect

**edits**. Put a timed effect on whatever primary clip is playing at given timeline moments: zoomPunch, impactShake, flashHits or vibrate at each time, or smoothZoom / rackFocus starting at the time. Times already on the clip are kept, so you can add moments one at a time.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | yes |  | zoomPunch, impactShake, flashHits, vibrate, smoothZoom or rackFocus |
| `times` | number[] | yes |  | Timeline seconds |
| `params` | object |  |  | Other params of the effect, e.g. {amount: 0.2} |
| `sound` | boolean \| string |  | `false` | true = the matching sound (hit for zoomPunch and flashHits, impact for impactShake, whoosh for smoothZoom) peaking at each moment, or a sound effect id |

### list_sound_effects

**read-only**. List the built-in sound effects (whoosh, swoosh, riser, glitch, impact, hit, bass drop, pop, click, notification, error, typing, ding, success, shutter, heartbeat).

_No parameters._

### add_sound_effect

**edits**. Add a sound effect at timeline moments where something visibly happens: a pop when text appears, an impact on a reveal, a riser ending on a drop. A sound with nothing on screen to match feels random: for transitions use set_transition with sound, for zoom punches and shakes use add_moment_effect with sound. align 'peak' (default) lines the loudest point up with the time, 'end' makes the sound finish there (risers), 'start' begins it there.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | yes |  | Sound effect id (see list_sound_effects) |
| `times` | number[] | yes |  | Timeline seconds |
| `align` | "peak" \| "start" \| "end" |  | `"peak"` |  |
| `volume` | number |  | `0.8` | (≥ 0, ≤ 4) |
| `params` | object |  |  |  |

## Transcript & captions

### transcribe

**edits**. Transcribe an asset's speech with word timings. Enables captions, transcript search and filler removal. Runs a Whisper model on this machine unless the session has another provider (no API key; the model downloads once, then works offline). Takes roughly real time on a CPU. Names often come out wrong: save them first with fix_transcript vocabulary, and the result lists likely mishearings to correct.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | yes |  |  |
| `language` | string |  |  | Language code such as 'en' or 'fr'; omit to detect |

### set_transcript

**edits**. Attach a transcript to an asset from SRT, VTT, Whisper/Deepgram/AssemblyAI JSON, or {words:[{text,start,end}]}. Times are in source seconds.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | yes |  |  |
| `content` | string \| object | yes |  |  |
| `format` | "srt" \| "vtt" \| "whisper" \| "deepgram" \| "assemblyai" \| "transcript" |  |  |  |

### get_transcript

**read-only**. Read an asset's transcript as timestamped sentences (source time) with speaking stats.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | yes |  |  |

### fix_transcript

**edits**. Correct words the speech recognizer got wrong, keeping their timings: find and replace words or phrases ("cloud" to "Claude", "cooper netties" to "Kubernetes") in one transcript or all of them. Matching ignores case and punctuation; punctuation around a match is kept. Captions, search and text-based cuts all use the corrected words. vocabulary saves the names and terms said in the video: transcribe passes them to recognizers that take hints, and this tool and transcribe list words that look like mishearings of them, so you can confirm each before replacing. An empty replace removes words from the transcript only (the video is not cut).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string |  |  | Transcript to fix (default: every transcript) |
| `replace` | { find, replace }[] |  | `[]` | Applied in order |
| `vocabulary` | string[] |  |  | Names and terms said in the video; replaces the saved list |

### search_transcript

**read-only**. Find where a phrase is said. Returns source times and, if that part is in the edit, timeline times.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes |  |  |
| `assetId` | string |  |  |  |

### find_retakes

**read-only**. Read a transcribed recording sentence by sentence and find retakes (a line said again because the first try had a slip, or a sentence abandoned and restarted) and repeats (several sentences in a row saying nearly the same thing). Lists every sentence with its number and source time, the groups found and the suggested sentence to keep. Read the sentences yourself too: you judge meaning better than word overlap. Then use remove_retakes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | yes |  |  |

### remove_retakes

**edits**. Cut whole sentences out of a transcribed recording, cleanly: each cut runs from just after the previous kept word to just before the next one, so the pause goes too and no kept word is clipped. Without `sentences`, removes what find_retakes suggests. Sentence numbers come from find_retakes. Layers, music and captions stay in sync.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | yes |  |  |
| `sentences` | integer[] |  |  | Sentence numbers to remove (default: the suggested retakes and repeats) |

### cleanup_speech

**edits**. Tighten talking-head footage using its transcript: cut filler words (um, uh…), stutters and long pauses. Layers and audio shift to stay in sync.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | yes |  |  |
| `fillers` | boolean \| string[] |  | `true` | true = default list, or a custom list (e.g. add 'like', 'you know') |
| `repetitions` | boolean |  | `true` |  |
| `maxPause` | number |  | `0.6` | Pauses longer than this are shortened (> 0) |
| `keepPause` | number |  | `0.2` | Pause left behind (≥ 0) |

### cut_ranges

**edits**. Remove time ranges from the finished timeline (timeline seconds). Everything after each cut moves earlier.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ranges` | { start, end }[] | yes |  |  |

### assemble_from_source

**edits**. Rebuild the primary track from chosen source ranges of one asset, in the order given (e.g. pick the best moments of a long recording by transcript).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | yes |  |  |
| `ranges` | { start, end }[] | yes |  |  |
| `transition` | { type, duration, origin } |  |  |  |
| `transition.type` | string | yes |  | Transition id from the transitions catalog, e.g. 'fade', 'slideleft' |
| `transition.duration` | number |  | `0.5` | (> 0, ≤ 5) |
| `transition.origin` | { x, y } |  |  | Where shape transitions such as circlereveal start (frame fractions; default center) |
| `transition.origin.x` | number | yes |  | (≥ 0, ≤ 1) |
| `transition.origin.y` | number | yes |  | (≥ 0, ≤ 1) |
| `fit` | "cover" \| "contain" \| "stretch" \| "blur" |  |  | cover = fill & crop, contain = letterbox, stretch = distort, blur = contain over blurred copy |

### set_captions

**edits**. Turn captions on/off and pick a style (see list_caption_styles). Captions come from transcripts and stay synced through edits. Override style fields like position (0-1), fontSize, highlightColor, uppercase, maxWordsPerLine.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean |  | `true` |  |
| `style` | string |  |  |  |
| `overrides` | object |  |  |  |
| `segments` | { text, start, end }[] |  |  | Manual captions in timeline seconds (instead of transcripts) |

### export_captions

**read-only**. Write the captions as a subtitle sidecar file (srt, vtt or ass), e.g. for YouTube upload.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | "srt" \| "vtt" \| "ass" |  | `"srt"` |  |
| `output` | string |  |  |  |

## Voice

### list_voices

**read-only**. List the narration voices: the local voices that run on this machine (with language or accent, gender and quality grade) and the session's own provider if it has one. Grades are the voice model's published ones; prefer A to C+ for English narration. Besides English there are Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian and Brazilian Portuguese voices (they need the optional espeak-ng package); write the text in that language.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `all` | boolean |  | `false` | Include weaker voices (graded below C+) |
| `language` | string |  |  | Only voices speaking this language, e.g. 'es', 'fr' or 'French' |

### preview_voice

**read-only**. Speak a sample line in one or more voices and save each as a WAV file to listen to and compare, without changing the project. Use the actual opening line of the script, so the choice is made on real material.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `voices` | string[] | yes |  | Voice ids to audition |
| `text` | string |  | `"Here are five quick tips that will change how you use your phone."` | Line to speak |
| `speed` | number |  |  |  |

### set_voice

**edits**. Set the project's narration voice and speed, used by generate_voiceover and revoice when no voice is given. Use revoice with all=true to apply it to narration already in the project.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `voice` | string | yes |  |  |
| `speed` | number |  |  | (≥ 0.5, ≤ 2) |

### generate_voiceover

**edits**. Synthesize narration from text and add it as a voice-over with measured word timings for captions. Runs a neural voice on this machine unless the session has another provider (no API key; the model downloads once). Pick a voice with list_voices and audition it with preview_voice; the project's default voice (set_voice) is used when none is given. Write it the way people talk, in short sentences; one call per section lets you place each part on the timeline. Pacing markup (local voice): [pause] (0.6s) or [pause 1.5] for a pause, [breath] for a short one, [slow]...[/slow] and [fast]...[/fast] for pace, *word* to set a word apart. The text is spoken in the voice's language (list_voices shows it).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes |  | What to say, with optional pacing markup |
| `start` | number |  | `0` | (≥ 0) |
| `voice` | string |  |  | Voice id (see list_voices); default: the project's voice, else af_heart |
| `speed` | number |  |  | 1 = normal, 1.1 a little brisker |
| `instructions` | string |  |  | Delivery style, e.g. 'warm and upbeat' (only for an optional external voice provider; the local voice ignores it) |
| `volume` | number |  | `1` |  |

### revoice

**edits**. Re-generate narration already in the project with a new voice, speed or wording, keeping each voice-over where it is on the timeline. Target one voice-over (its audio clip id or asset id), or all=true for every narration made with generate_voiceover. New wording changes the length: check what follows and the graphics timed to words.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string |  |  | Voice-over audio clip id or asset id |
| `all` | boolean |  | `false` |  |
| `voice` | string |  |  | Default: the project's voice |
| `speed` | number |  |  |  |
| `text` | string |  |  | New wording (one target only) |

## Color & looks

### color_adjust

**edits**. Color correct and grade a clip, a media layer, every clip, or the whole video. Settings merge into the target's existing color settings, so you can tweak one control at a time. Light: exposure (stops), brightness, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, brilliance. Color: temperature, tint, hue (degrees), saturation, vibrance, hsl per color (red, orange, yellow, green, aqua, blue, purple, magenta). Grading: curves (master/red/green/blue point graphs or a preset), wheels (shadows/midtones/highlights tint). Finish: fade, clarity, sharpen, vignette, grain, autoCorrect. Most sliders are -100..100 with 0 = unchanged. Correct first (exposure, white balance, contrast), then grade. Use analyze_color and render_scopes to check the result.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string |  | `"global"` | "global" (whole video), "all-clips", a clip id, or a media layer id |
| `settings` | { exposure, brightness, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, brilliance, temperature, tint, hue, saturation, vibrance, hsl, curves, wheels, fade, clarity, sharpen, vignette, grain, autoCorrect } |  | `{}` |  |
| `settings.exposure` | number |  |  | Exposure in stops (-3..3) (≥ -3, ≤ 3) |
| `settings.brightness` | number |  |  | Overall brightness (≥ -100, ≤ 100) |
| `settings.contrast` | number |  |  | Contrast (≥ -100, ≤ 100) |
| `settings.highlights` | number |  |  | Recover (−) or boost (+) bright areas (≥ -100, ≤ 100) |
| `settings.shadows` | number |  |  | Lift (+) or deepen (−) dark areas (≥ -100, ≤ 100) |
| `settings.whites` | number |  |  | Set the white point: + brighter whites, − pull whites down (≥ -100, ≤ 100) |
| `settings.blacks` | number |  |  | Set the black point: + lifted blacks, − crushed blacks (≥ -100, ≤ 100) |
| `settings.brilliance` | number |  |  | Balance the image: + brightens shadows and tames highlights, − adds punch (≥ -100, ≤ 100) |
| `settings.temperature` | number |  |  | White balance: − cooler/blue, + warmer/yellow (≥ -100, ≤ 100) |
| `settings.tint` | number |  |  | White balance: − greener, + more magenta (≥ -100, ≤ 100) |
| `settings.hue` | number |  |  | Rotate all hues in degrees (≥ -180, ≤ 180) |
| `settings.saturation` | number |  |  | Saturation of all colors (−100 = black & white) (≥ -100, ≤ 100) |
| `settings.vibrance` | number |  |  | Smart saturation: boosts muted colors more than already-saturated ones and protects skin (≥ -100, ≤ 100) |
| `settings.hsl` | { red, orange, yellow, green, aqua, blue, purple, magenta } |  |  | Per-color hue/saturation/luminance, e.g. {blue: {saturation: 30}, orange: {luminance: 10}} |

### get_color

**read-only**. Read the current color settings of a target ("global", a clip id, or a media layer id).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string |  | `"global"` |  |

### analyze_color

**read-only**. Measure the edited video's color at a time: average brightness, shadow/highlight levels, contrast range, saturation and color cast, with plain-language suggestions. Use before and after color_adjust.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `time` | number |  |  | Timeline time; defaults to the middle of the video (≥ 0) |

### sample_color

**read-only**. Measure the average color of a small area of a source video or image at a source time, e.g. a green screen before chromaKey, or a brand color to match text and section cards to. x, y are frame fractions of the area's center.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | yes |  |  |
| `time` | number |  | `0` | Source seconds (≥ 0) |
| `x` | number | yes |  | (≥ 0, ≤ 1) |
| `y` | number | yes |  | (≥ 0, ≤ 1) |
| `size` | number |  | `0.02` | Square side as a fraction of the frame width (≥ 0.002, ≤ 0.5) |

### render_scopes

**read-only**. Render video scopes (histogram, luma waveform, RGB parade, vectorscope) for the frame at a time and look at them, like a colorist would.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `time` | number |  |  | (≥ 0) |
| `scopes` | "histogram" \| "waveform" \| "parade" \| "vectorscope"[] |  |  |  |

### set_color_space

**edits**. Say what color space a video or picture was recorded in, so it renders as its maker defines it: camera log (flat, gray-looking footage) and HDR are converted to the edit's Rec.709 with the maker's published curve and gamut, through ACES with a filmic highlight roll-off. Set it before grading log footage: color_adjust's exposure, temperature, tint, contrast, saturation and wheels then grade on scene light (in ACEScct, inside the conversion), the rest of the panel on the finished picture. HDR files tagged as HLG or PQ are set when imported. For delivery without banding after heavy grades, render_video with bitDepth 10. Log footage is usually tagged Rec.709, so look at it first (render_frame, render_scopes): a flat, low-contrast picture with no deep blacks and no bright whites is likely log. When the camera is unknown, offer_choices with a frame converted with the two or three likeliest spaces. Spaces: "rec709" (Rec.709: Ordinary video (phones, most cameras, screen recordings, the web). The default: the picture is used as it is.); "srgb" (sRGB: Pictures and graphics made for screens. Used as it is.); "slog3-sgamut3cine" (Sony S-Log3 / S-Gamut3.Cine: Sony cameras (FX3, FX6, A7S III, Venice) shot in S-Log3 with S-Gamut3.Cine: flat, gray-looking footage, 18% gray near 41%.); "slog3-sgamut3" (Sony S-Log3 / S-Gamut3: Sony S-Log3 with the wider S-Gamut3.); "vlog-vgamut" (Panasonic V-Log / V-Gamut: Panasonic cameras (GH5S, GH6, S1H, S5) shot in V-Log: flat footage, 18% gray near 42%.); "applelog" (Apple Log: iPhone 15 Pro and later recording in Apple Log (ProRes Log): very flat footage, 18% gray near 49%, Rec.2020 primaries.); "logc3-awg3" (ARRI LogC3 / ALEXA Wide Gamut 3: ARRI ALEXA cameras before the ALEXA 35 (LogC3 at EI 800): 18% gray near 39%.); "logc4-awg4" (ARRI LogC4 / ALEXA Wide Gamut 4: ARRI ALEXA 35 footage: 18% gray near 28%.); "clog3-cinemagamut" (Canon Log 3 / Cinema Gamut: Canon cameras (C70, C300 Mark III, R5 C, R5, R6 II) shot in Canon Log 3: flat footage, 18% gray near 34%.); "bmdfilm-gen5" (Blackmagic Film Gen 5: Blackmagic cameras (Pocket 4K/6K, URSA) in Film mode, Generation 5 color science: 18% gray near 38%.); "hlg-rec2020" (HLG (Rec.2020): HDR video in HLG, as phones and cameras record HDR (often tagged arib-std-b67).); "pq-rec2020" (PQ / HDR10 (Rec.2020): HDR video in PQ (HDR10, Dolby Vision base layers; tagged smpte2084).). "rec709" sets it back to ordinary video.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetIds` | string[] | yes |  | Video or picture assets recorded in this space |
| `colorSpace` | "rec709" \| "srgb" \| "slog3-sgamut3cine" \| "slog3-sgamut3" \| "vlog-vgamut" \| "applelog" \| "logc3-awg3" \| "logc4-awg4" \| "clog3-cinemagamut" \| "bmdfilm-gen5" \| "hlg-rec2020" \| "pq-rec2020" | yes |  |  |

### apply_look

**edits**. Give a clip, a media layer, every clip or the whole video a finished film look: a grade plus film effects (print-film curve, halation, bloom, anamorphic flare, film grain, gate weave), placed after the edit's own grade so color_adjust still corrects underneath. Applying another look replaces this one; "none" removes it. strength (0..1) scales the whole look. Correct exposure and white balance first, then pick a look that suits the content, and check it with render_frame. Looks: "blockbuster" (Teal and orange blockbuster: Warm skin against teal shadows and backgrounds, punchy contrast, a print-like curve and fine grain: the big action and adventure look. Best with people in the frame; heavy on scenes without skin.); "warm-70s-print" (Warm 70s print: Faded, warm and soft: lifted blacks, golden highlights, coarse grain, glowing highlights and a slight gate weave, like a projected print from the seventies. For nostalgia, memories, travel and music videos.); "cold-thriller" (Cold thriller: Cool, desaturated and contrasty, with green-teal shadows: tension, crime, sci-fi and night interiors. Skin goes pale; avoid for warm or friendly content.); "bleach-bypass" (Bleach bypass: Silvery, low saturation and hard contrast, as when the bleach step is skipped in film processing: gritty war, drama and sports. Strong; lower the strength for a hint of it.); "dreamy" (Dreamy glow: Soft, bright and warm, with glowing highlights and gentle contrast: weddings, romance, beauty and slow, peaceful moments.); "night-anamorphic" (Anamorphic night: Cool night with horizontal blue streaks through the lights and medium grain: city streets, cars and neon. Needs bright points of light in the frame to show its streaks.). For one effect on its own (halation, bloom, anamorphicFlare, filmGrain, gateWeave, printFilm, lensDistortion), use add_effect.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string |  | `"all-clips"` | "all-clips", "global" (the whole video, after the clips are joined), a clip id or a media layer id |
| `look` | string | yes |  | A look id, or "none" to remove the look |
| `strength` | number |  | `1` | How much of the look (0..1) (≥ 0, ≤ 1) |

### match_color

**edits**. Make clips look like a reference clip, so shots from different cameras or lighting cut together. Each shot's colors are measured on three frames and matched to the reference's as one color transfer (lightness, cast, saturation and hue together, with skin kept on the skin line), or with per-channel curves when those match better; the method that comes closest on a held-out frame wins. The match is a colorMatch effect at the end of each clip (re-running replaces it), before any whole-video grade. For several scenes at once, or a reference still, use grade_scene. Check with render_frame, and lower strength if it overshoots.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipIds` | string[] | yes |  | Clips to change, or ["all-clips"] for every clip except the reference |
| `referenceClipId` | string | yes |  | Clip whose look to match |
| `strength` | number |  | `0.85` | (≥ 0, ≤ 1) |
| `method` | "auto" \| "transfer" \| "reinhard" \| "curves" |  | `"auto"` | auto tries each and keeps the closest; transfer (Oklab color transfer), reinhard (mean and spread), curves (per-channel) |

### grade_scene

**edits**. Match shots to a hero shot or a reference still, one scene at a time: for each scene, every listed clip is matched to its reference (a clip id, or the id of an imported image such as a frame from a film the user names). Use after detect_scenes and a look at the shots (render_contact_sheet): pick the best-looking shot of each scene as its reference, grade that one first with color_adjust, then match the rest to it. Each shot's colors are measured on three frames and three methods are fitted (an Oklab color transfer, a Reinhard mean and spread transfer, per-channel curves); the one closest to the reference on a held-out frame wins, hue turns are held to maxHueShift, and skin found by face detection stays on the vectorscope skin line. The report gives each shot's color difference to its reference (ΔE 2000; under 2 is a close match, over 6 a clear mismatch) before and after. Check the result with render_frame or render_scopes; lower strength if a match looks forced.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scenes` | { reference, clips }[] | yes |  |  |
| `strength` | number |  | `0.85` | (≥ 0, ≤ 1) |
| `method` | "auto" \| "transfer" \| "reinhard" \| "curves" |  | `"auto"` | auto tries each and keeps the closest; transfer (Oklab color transfer), reinhard (mean and spread), curves (per-channel) |
| `maxHueShift` | number |  | `15` | Largest hue turn allowed, degrees (raise only when asked for a strong color change) (≥ 0, ≤ 180) |

### grade_region

**edits**. Secondary color correction: grade only part of the frame, as a colorist does after the primary grade. Deepen a sky, warm or lift faces, cool the shadows, tame bright highlights, make one colored object pop. The mask selects the part: key (an HSL qualifier: hue range in degrees, saturation and luma ranges, with softness), luma (a brightness range: highlights or shadows), shape (an ellipse, rectangle or polygon; moved with keyframes, or pinned to a tracked surface with pin_mask), face (soft ellipses following every face), person (the person's cutout), sky, object (select_object) or depth (a range of distance, see estimate_depth: grade the background apart from the subject); these five work on primary video clips only. Masks combine (a blue key intersected with a shape over the top of the frame selects sky without blue clothes), invert, grow or shrink, and feather. color takes the same settings as color_adjust. Each correction has a label; the same label updates it (color settings merge, a new mask replaces the old), and remove: true deletes it. Work in this order: render_mask to check the selection at the start, middle and end of the clip (and at fast motion), then grade, then render_frame and render_scopes to check for edges and clipping. Keep feather at 0.01 or more so the edge never shows.

| `mask` | { kind, object, hue, saturation, luma, distance, softness, shape, invert, feather, grow, smooth, denoise, combine } |  |  | What to grade; needed for a new correction, omit to keep the current mask |
| `mask.kind` | "person" \| "face" \| "object" \| "sky" \| "depth" \| "key" \| "luma" \| "shape" | yes |  | person = the person's cutout, face = soft ellipses following every face, object = a tracked object from select_object, sky = the sky, depth = a range of distance (all five found per frame by a model; primary video clips only), key = an HSL qualifier on hue, saturation and luma ranges, luma = a brightness range only, shape = an ellipse, rectangle or polygon, fixed, moving with keyframes, or pinned to a track |

### render_mask

**read-only**. Look at a mask before (or after) grading or compositing with it: renders the frame with the mask as white on black (matte) or as a red tint over the picture (overlay). Give a mask to try one, or the label of a masked effect on the target (from grade_region). The mask is cut from the picture as it reaches that effect. A good mask covers the whole subject with no holes, leaves everything else black, has a soft but tight edge, and holds at the start, middle and end of the clip and during fast motion: check several times.
